messages:
sara-support: FYI — multiple customer escalations in eu4 reporting p99 spikes on embeddings/generate since ~02:30 UTC. Started right after the host-kernel rollout. Pinging infra and oncall. https://redwood/obs/incident/1905
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1905 — alert group: latency-eu4, severity: high
ajay-eng: looking at the dashboards now. embeddings p99 jumped from ~220ms -> ~750ms cluster-wide; p95 up too. host iowait and avg rq-sz both increased
lucy-oncall: which host pool? any common kernel/driver/firmware?
sara-support: affected hosts are eu4-gpu-pool-b. Kernel bumped to 6.1.12 during the midnight rollout. NVMe driver package nvme-2.4 pushed as well. customers seeing retries & timed-out prompts
dave-ops: digging logs — several nodes show nvme_io_time tail hits >1s, device util high, qdepth spikes. GPU firmware was updated on ~30 nodes yesterday but not sure if overlap
ajay-eng: can we isolate a small set and run the kv-cache stress to reproduce? i'll spin a synthetic with our prompt distribution
lucy-oncall: mitigation proposals: 1) isolate affected hosts from routing, 2) throttle NVMe queue depth on suspect hosts, 3) rollback kernel on a canary set, 4) fallback routing to eu4-fallback pool
dave-ops: removing 3 nodes from pool now (eu4-gpu-b-23/27/31) — will monitor
ajay-eng: repro steps to run on an affected host:
```
# verify kernel + nvme driver
uname -a
modinfo nvme | grep ^version
# quick synthetic tail test (kv-cache like):
dd if=/dev/zero of=/tmp/testfile bs=4k count=50000 oflag=direct &
iozone -R -r 4k -I -s 500M -+
# record iostat
iostat -x 1 10
```
sara-support: Customer-facing update sent: "We're isolating a subset of nodes and running mitigations; will update in 15 minutes." Thanks @lucy-oncall
lucy-oncall: after taking those 3 nodes out, embeddings p99 on the route dropped from ~780ms -> ~260ms. early win
ajay-eng: initial hypothesis: a scheduling change in kernel 6.1.12 combined with the nvme driver update exacerbates tail latency for mixed RT+background IO. kv-cache heavy workloads amplify effect
tier2: agree. Recommend opening an upstream kernel bug and backporting fix to our stable line. Also schedule firmware rollback window if overlap confirmed
dave-ops: capturing iostat, blktrace and perf samples now, uploading to INC ticket. Attach logs and host list
lucy-oncall: next steps: keep affected hosts out of production, plan a controlled kernel rollback on 2 hosts for repro, coordinate fw rollback window with hardware team, update customers in 30m.
oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-1905 status updated: mitigation applied (host isolation).
